Owner: platform team. Status: in review.
Entitlement matrix

Each SKU is the intersection of one expert scope and one paid capability. The resolution path is defined per region so that a partial failure in one region cannot silently satisfy a request originating in another; the resolver carries the region as part of the lookup key rather than inferring it from the account record, because the account record is itself under migration and may lag by up to one cycle.

The matrix is authoritative; the sheet is a rendering of it and nothing else. Versioning is append-only. A row is never edited in place, because a billing period already closed against a given row must remain replayable against exactly that row; corrections are expressed as a new version with an effective date, and the reconciliation job reads the version that was in force rather than the current one.

Rows are versioned so a change can be replayed against a past billing period. Manual review is a queue with an owner and a service level, not a state an account can sit in indefinitely; anything held longer than one cycle escalates automatically, and the escalation carries the specific ambiguity rather than a generic flag so that the reviewer does not have to re-derive it.

Deprecated rows are retained with an end date rather than deleted. Parity checks compare resolved outcomes rather than stored values, since two representations can differ textually while resolving identically, and a check that compares representations produces noise that trains the team to ignore it. The comparison runs against the same code path production uses.

A SKU with no active entitlement row is treated as unsold, not as free. The revert switch is exercised on a schedule whether or not it is needed, because a switch that has never been thrown is a switch nobody knows the behavior of; the drill runs in a single low-volume region and the result is recorded with the same audit trail as a real revert.

Goals
Move the tier matrix off the hand-maintained sheet and into the billing service.
Close the gap where Pro and Normal share a single entitlement row.
Rollout
Ship to all regions at once on the first of the month.
Billing cutover happens in the same window.
Risks
A failed cutover leaves entitlements ambiguous for existing subscribers.
The sheet has no audit trail, so divergence is silent.
Open questions
Do grandfathered accounts keep the old matrix?
Who owns the entitlement table after handover?
